theorem lt_or_fuzzy_of_lf {x y : PGame} : x ⧏ y → x < y ∨ x ‖ y :=
  lf_iff_lt_or_fuzzy.1

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
@[symm]
theorem Fuzzy.swap {x y : PGame} : x ‖ y → y ‖ x :=
  And.symm

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
alias Fuzzy.lf := lf_of_fuzzy

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
theorem Fuzzy.not_equiv {x y : PGame} (h : x ‖ y) : ¬(x ≈ y) := fun h' => h'.1.not_gf h.2

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
theorem not_fuzzy_of_ge {x y : PGame} (h : y ≤ x) : ¬x ‖ y := fun h' => h'.1.not_ge h

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
theorem fuzzy_congr {x₁ y₁ x₂ y₂ : PGame} (hx : x₁ ≈ x₂) (hy : y₁ ≈ y₂) : x₁ ‖ y₁ ↔ x₂ ‖ y₂ :=
  show _ ∧ _ ↔ _ ∧ _ by rw [lf_congr hx hy, lf_congr hy hx]

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
lemma Identical.le : ∀ {x y}, x ≡ y → x ≤ y
  | mk _ _ _ _, mk _ _ _ _, ⟨hL, hR⟩ => le_of_forall_lf
    (fun i ↦ let ⟨_, hj⟩ := hL.1 i; lf_of_le_moveLeft hj.le)
    (fun i ↦ let ⟨_, hj⟩ := hR.2 i; lf_of_moveRight_le hj.le)

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
theorem fuzzy_congr_imp {x₁ y₁ x₂ y₂ : PGame} (hx : x₁ ≈ x₂) (hy : y₁ ≈ y₂) : x₁ ‖ y₁ → x₂ ‖ y₂ :=
  (fuzzy_congr hx hy).1

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.Nim
theorem nim_fuzzy_zero_of_ne_zero {o : Ordinal} (ho : o ≠ 0) : nim o ‖ 0 := by
  rw [Impartial.fuzzy_zero_iff_lf, lf_zero_le]
  use toRightMovesNim ⟨0, Ordinal.pos_iff_ne_zero.2 ho⟩
  simp

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
@[trans]
theorem fuzzy_of_fuzzy_of_equiv {x y z : PGame} (h₁ : x ‖ y) (h₂ : y ≈ z) : x ‖ z :=
  (fuzzy_congr_right h₂).1 h₁

--src: Mathlib.Data.Nat.ModEq
lemma of_dvd (d : m ∣ n) (h : a ≡ b [MOD n]) : a ≡ b [MOD m] :=
  modEq_of_dvd <| Int.ofNat_dvd.mpr d |>.trans h.dvd

--src: Mathlib.Data.Nat.ModEq
theorem mod_lcm (hn : a ≡ b [MOD n]) (hm : a ≡ b [MOD m]) : a ≡ b [MOD lcm n m] :=
  Nat.modEq_iff_dvd.mpr <| Int.lcm_dvd (Nat.modEq_iff_dvd.mp hn) (Nat.modEq_iff_dvd.mp hm)

--src: Mathlib.Data.Nat.ModEq
@[trans]
protected theorem trans : a ≡ b [MOD n] → b ≡ c [MOD n] → a ≡ c [MOD n] :=
  Eq.trans

--src: Mathlib.Data.Nat.ModEq
lemma modEq_one : a ≡ b [MOD 1] := modEq_of_dvd <| one_dvd _

--src: Mathlib.Data.Nat.ModEq
protected theorem comm : a ≡ b [MOD n] ↔ b ≡ a [MOD n] :=
  ⟨ModEq.symm, ModEq.symm⟩

--src: Mathlib.Data.Int.ModEq
theorem mod_modEq (a n) : a % n ≡ a [ZMOD n] :=
  emod_emod _ _

--src: Mathlib.Data.Part
theorem mod_mem_mod [Mod α] (a b : Part α) (ma mb : α) (ha : ma ∈ a) (hb : mb ∈ b) :
    ma % mb ∈ a % b := by simp [mod_def]; aesop

--src: Mathlib.Data.Int.ModEq
theorem modEq_one : a ≡ b [ZMOD 1] :=
  modEq_of_dvd (one_dvd _)

--src: Mathlib.NumberTheory.LucasLehmer
theorem sZMod_eq_sMod (p : ℕ) (i : ℕ) : sZMod p i = (sMod p i : ZMod (2 ^ p - 1)) := by
  induction i <;> push_cast [← Int.coe_nat_two_pow_pred p, sMod, sZMod, *] <;> rfl

--src: Mathlib.Data.Nat.ModEq
@[simp] lemma add_modEq_right : a + n ≡ a [MOD n] := by rw [ModEq, add_mod_right]

  Nat.modEq_iff_dvd.mpr <| Int.lcm_dvd (Nat.modEq_iff_dvd.mp hn) (Nat.modEq_iff_dvd.mp hm)

theorem add_lf_add_right {y z : PGame} (h : y ⧏ z) (x) : y + x ⧏ z + x :=
  suffices z + x ≤ y + x → z ≤ y by
    rw [← PGame.not_le] at h ⊢
    exact mt this h
  fun w =>
  calc
    z ≤ z + 0 := (addZeroRelabelling _).symm.le
    _ ≤ z + (x + -x) := add_le_add_left (zero_le_add_neg_cancel x) _
    _ ≤ z + x + -x := (addAssocRelabelling _ _ _).symm.le
    _ ≤ y + x + -x := add_le_add_right w _
    _ ≤ y + (x + -x) := (addAssocRelabelling _ _ _).le
    _ ≤ y + 0 := add_le_add_left (add_neg_cancel_le_zero x) _

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a
